exercises.title: Remove the trailing comma
exercises.template:
{%- set methods = ["credit_card", "coupon", "bank_transfer", "gift_card"] -%}
select
    orderid as order_id,
    {%- for m in methods %}
    sum(case when paymentmethod = '{{ m }}' then amount else 0 end)
        as {{ m }}_amount,
    {%- endfor %}
from stripe.payments
where status = 'success'
group by orderid
order by orderid
exercises.task: The loop writes a comma after every column, also after the last one, and the SQL fails. Use loop.last so that the last column has no comma.

exercises.title: Write the cents_to_dollars macro

solution.template:
{% macro cents_to_dollars(column_name, decimals=2) -%}
    round({{ column_name }} / 100, {{ decimals }})
{%- endmacro %}
select
    id as payment_id,
    {{ cents_to_dollars('amount') }} as amount_usd,
    {{ cents_to_dollars('amount', 0) }} as amount_usd_rounded
from stripe.payments

exercises.task: Complete the macro: it must return round(<column> / 100, <decimals>).

goal.book:
select
    id as payment_id,
    round(amount / 100, 2) as amount_usd,
    round(amount / 100, 0) as amount_usd_rounded
from stripe.payments

exercises.hint: Inside the macro, write round({{ column_name }} / 100, {{ decimals }})
exercises.why: A macro is a function that returns text. Arguments can have default values (decimals=2).
exercises.derived: the book's template with the macro body removed

exercises.title: A total inside a loop
exercises.task: This template prints total=0: a set inside a loop does not change the variable outside. Use namespace() to get total=6.
exercises.hint: {% set ns = namespace(total=0) %} ... {% set ns.total = ns.total + x %}
exercises.why: Each loop iteration has its own scope. A namespace object is shared.
exercises.derived: the book says namespace() gives 6; the line total= is kept from its template

exercises.title: The pivot model of the project
exercises.task: Compile the model: the loop is unrolled and the ephemeral model int_payments__successful becomes a CTE. Then run it: one row per order with one column per payment method.

...
pivoted as (

    select
        order_id,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'bank_transfer' then amount else 0 end)
            as bank_transfer_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'coupon' then amount else 0 end)
            as coupon_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'credit_card' then amount else 0 end)
            as credit_card_amount,
        sum(case when payment_method = 'gift_card' then amount else 0 end)
            as gift_card_amount

    from payments

)

select * from pivoted

exercises.hint: Press Compile, then Run the compiled SQL.
exercises.why: ref() to an ephemeral model does not read a table: dbt pastes its SQL as a CTE named __dbt__cte__<model>.
